answer: Every new agent must lock a walnut of scarce compute credits before it can trade. Trading rights then grow only along a vine of vouchers: an established peer pledges part of its own lock to endorse a newcomer, and that pledge stays at risk until the first settlement window closes. Payouts, the network's nectar, are released only if no fraud is flagged; otherwise the voucher's pledge and the newcomer's lock are both slashed. A sybil farm must therefore pre-fund real bonds and recruit many at-risk endorsers, so each extra fake identity raises the attacker's cost.
